newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns AA local currency rating to Chile.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns AA local currency rating to Chile.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned a local currency rating of AA to the Republic of Chile.
"The rating applies to all senior, unsecured obligations of Chile denominated in pesos," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA pointed to the country's strong fiscal position, its low internal public debt, and its success in moderating inflation.

The agency said that 1996 will be Chile's thirteenth successive year of positive economic growth, its Central Government's tenth year of fiscal surplus, and the ninth year of surplus on the consolidated public sector accounts.
"These achievements attest to the quality of the economic bureaucracy, whose handling of macroeconomic policy is both exceptionally good and consensual," IBCA said.

"The fiscal accounts of the Central Government are heading for a surplus of 1.5 per cent of GDP this year, and it is estimated that the consolidated public sector accounts will also record a surplus in the region of one percent of GDP," the rating agency said.

It said in the recent past, the major area of public sector savings had been the interest bill, which the Government had managed to more than halve since 1990 by prepaying its external debt and using current surpluses to run down internal debt.
"The stock of Treasury debt currently in circulation is paltry, being below one percent of GDP," it said.

"The ratio of non-interest outlays to GDP has stayed more or less the same, as savings on pensions spending have been offset by rising social spending, particularly on health and education, with the ultimate aim of improving a disappointing record on income distribution," IBCA said.

"The Central Bank represents the only area of official finances which is regularly in deficit. This imbalance is rarely more than one percent of gdp and mainly reflects the cost of issuing debt to sterilise large inflows of foreign capital."
IBCA added that in this respect, the effect of the copper price fall induced by the Sumitomo scam, provided it does not go too far, should be generally supportive to the goals of economic policy.

"The sharp deterioration in the terms of external trade -- both because of the fall in copper prices and the strong rise in oil import prices this year -- appears to be helping to slow economic growth from potentially overheated levels while also reducing the Central Bank's burden of sterilisation," it said.
It said this should stem nominal growth in the Central Bank's stock of domestic debt.
"Moreover, in the second half of this year, the annual inflation rate has for the first time fallen convincingly below 8.0 percent," IBCA said.

"Although further improvements from the current level (of 6.2 per cent in October) are likely to prove difficult in the medium term, such progress as there has been should help to wean public sector workers off wage indexation that is backwards looking. This will add further support to public sector savings in the future."
